correctness.rationale: The model reduction is an exact sum and centered imbalance identity. Conservation and cooperative positivity give global existence, d<=0 and I<=epsilon exp(-kappa epsilon t). For fixed a>0 a variation-of-constants d bound gives an explicit O_a(sqrt epsilon) relative correction to Z^2/(2epsilon)=1. At a=0 the exact unique scalar final-size equation has quadratic curvature M2>1. Uniform-in-a exponentially decaying infectious tails for fixed epsilon rigorously prove continuity and distinguish iterated limits. The rational illustration M2=76/49 and ODE trend were checked; finite integration is not used as an asymptotic proof.

The main new claim is the pair of iterated limits and their explicit separation, not merely the known frozen-class formula.

originality.rationale: The primary Allen–Heller–Pons MB system treats reproduction-number thresholds and parameter sensitivities, not critical final-size amplitudes. Fixed-group final-size results (Magal–Seydi–Webb and El Attouga–El Khalifi) do not contain the positive bidirectional-turnover regime; prevalence-coupled fear models are structurally distinct. The joint noncommutation statement was not located in the actual semantic database queries, own recoverable claims, and searched primary literature; residual bibliographic risk remains.

value.rationale: The switching/non-switching singularity separates two biologically interpretable modeling regimes at exactly the same reproduction threshold. It quantifies a nonuniform critical epidemic-size response to arbitrarily slow behavioral mobility by sharp, parameter-transparent coefficients, rather than an incidental finite numerical difference. This directly matters when replacing changing behavioral risk classes by fixed susceptibility strata.
